books.section: Topic 4.7 Expanding Democracy, A. Participatory Democracy and an Expanding Electorate
The Whig Party and the Second Party System

stimulus.text: The lithograph shows General William Henry Harrison in military uniform, with a wreath below naming him “of Tippecanoe, Fort Meigs and the Thames.” Published in 1840. In that year the Whigs nominated Harrison, a hero of the War of 1812, for president. After a colorful campaign, which included the catchy slogan “Tippecanoe and Tyler Too,” Harrison was elected. He died a month after taking office, and Vice President John Tyler became the first vice president to succeed to office after the death of a president. (Paraphrase of 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 13.)
stimulus.source_note: Lithograph “General Wm. H. Harrison of Tippecanoe, Fort Meigs and the Thames,” published 1840 (Library of Congress). Public domain; text paraphrases 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 13. Viewed before writing.

stem: Tyler succeeding Harrison after one month mattered most because it was

options.text: the first time a Democrat became president of the United States
options.misconception: Tyler was a Whig, and Democrats had held the presidency before him.
Congress did not choose Tyler; he claimed the office as vice president.

options.text: the first vice-presidential succession after a president's death

options.misconception: No new election was called; Tyler served out Harrison's term.

rationales.A: Tyler was a Whig, not a Democrat.
rationales.B: Tyler claimed the office himself; Congress did not pick him.
rationales.C: No president had died in office before, so Tyler's claim to full presidential powers set the precedent.
rationales.D: Tyler served out the term; no new election was held.
rationales.general:
1. Check the first. No president had died in office before Harrison.
2. Check the rule. The Constitution said the vice president should take over, but not whether he was fully president.
3. Watch Tyler. He took the oath and claimed the full powers, setting the pattern.
Background: Harrison died a month after his inauguration in 1841, and Tyler served the rest of the term.
Remember: firsts matter because the first person to face a gap writes the rule.
